submission.justification: Module-D1 at 30% wall coverage gives the highest light collection of the three designs at the coverage limit: 51.1 PE/MeV (100k events), versus 37.5 for D2 and 25.3 for D3 at the same coverage. This is consistent with the 2025 summary (D1 38 PE/MeV at 20%, scaling roughly as coverage^0.8). 30% is the upper bound of the allowed range, and the 2026-01-20 meeting notes confirm enough feedthroughs for up to 30% coverage. Cold electronics are validated for all candidate designs. Robustness is the main open point: the documents do not contain a robustness assessment of D1's large-area light guide and bonded dichroic filter. Since modules cannot be accessed after fill, this should be verified (e.g., thermal-cycling and bond-integrity tests at cryogenic temperature) before the design freeze in Q3.

requirements.evidence: Simulated at 30%: D1 51.1, D2 37.5, D3 25.3 PE/MeV; D1 is the highest.

requirements.requirement: Module must be one of the three candidate designs
requirements.evidence: Module-D1 (large-area light guide with thin bonded dichroic filter) from candidate_specs.md.

requirements.requirement: Modules must be robust (inaccessible after cryostat fill)
requirements.evidence: No document assesses D1 mechanical or cryogenic robustness. The bonded dichroic filter is a potential failure mode. Requires cryogenic thermal-cycling and bond-integrity validation before freeze.
Coverage set to 30%, the upper limit of the allowed range.
